questions.q: A stranger sends you a QR code and says: 'Scan it and enter your PIN to receive ₹2,000.'
questions.why: Entering your PIN always sends money out. You never need a PIN to receive money.

questions.q: You scan a shopkeeper's QR at a petrol pump, check the name shown, and enter your PIN to pay for fuel.
questions.why: You started this payment yourself and paid a known merchant. Entering a PIN to pay is normal. Always check the receiver's name first.

questions.q: A caller says 'I'm from your bank. Your KYC expires today. Please tell me the OTP just sent to you.'
questions.why: Banks never ask for OTPs on a call. The fear of 'expiring today' is the trick.

questions.q: Your bank app shows a notification that you can update KYC. You open the official app yourself and follow the steps.
questions.why: You went to the official app on your own. Nobody pressured you or asked for an OTP.

questions.q: A 'customer care agent' asks you to install AnyDesk to fix a failed payment.
questions.why: Remote apps let scammers see your screen and OTPs and move money from your phone.

questions.q: A buyer on a marketplace app says: 'I'll pay you. Approve the request I sent to receive the money.'
questions.why: Approving a collect request pays the other person. Real buyers only need your UPI ID.

questions.q: A WhatsApp message with a file named 'RTO_Challan.apk' says you must install it to pay a traffic fine.
questions.why: An .apk sent over chat is almost always spyware. Governments don't send apps over WhatsApp.

questions.q: Your friend, standing next to you, asks you to send ₹200 to his UPI ID for snacks and you check his name on screen.
questions.why: You know the person, you can see them, and the payment is small and expected.

questions.q: Someone you don't know sends ₹5,000 'by mistake' and begs you to send it back to a different number right now.
questions.why: The money may be from a fraud and can be reversed. Return it only through your bank, never to a new number.

questions.q: A video caller in a police uniform says a parcel in your name has drugs and you must stay on the call and not tell your family.
questions.why: 'Digital arrest' does not exist. Police never arrest by video call or ask you to keep it secret.
